newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX oil complex ends higher on Iraqi events.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX oil complex ends higher on Iraqi events.

text.p: NYMEX October crude ended Tuesday at a closing high after heightened tension in Iraq propelled the oil complex higher, traders said.
"There were reports that Iraqi troops were massing in the south and that just set off a round of buying," said Jim Ritterbusch, a trader with Sweeney Oil.
October crude settled up 39 cents at $24.12 a barrel, after almost reaching its life-of-contract high of $24.25.
"We should break it (the life-of-contract high) within a few days," said Ritterbusch.
The next level of resistance is pegged at around $24.75.
Heating oil and gasoline followed crude higher ahead of weekly data on oil inventories by the American Petroleum Institute expected Tuesday evening.
October heating oil closed up 0.72 cent to 66.67 cents a gallon, and October gasoline closed up 0.76 cent to 64.85 cents a gallon.

Earlier Tuesday, a U.S. defense official denied a report citing Shiite muslim groups' claims that Iraq was massing troops near its southern border. Meanhwile, Iraq said it fired missiles at U.S. planes policing the southern no-fly zone.
While uncertainty surrounding the Iraqi conflict is supporting crude prices, traders said crude's price direction Wednesday will depend in part on this evening's API data.
"If there is a build of over 2.5 million barrels in distillates, this market may be seen at its top," said a trader.
The oil complex's uptrend has been fueled in part by a rally in heating oil prices that was ignited by low distillate stocks.
Last week, the API said distillate stocks grew 3.24 million barrels. Traders said consecutive inventory builds may signal a trend to rebuild stocks to more normal levels.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
